During the pandemic, however, the duo decided to shutter their label, before reemerging with a triumphant comeback show at New York Fashion Week this February.

I was thoroughly impressed with what I saw—a proposal for a complete modern wardrobe, full of familiar silhouettes tweaked just enough to feel genuinely fresh. There were boxy dress shirts, made in New York with luxurious Japanese cotton-silk blends, with large French cuffs finished with a single mother-of-pearl button in lieu of a cufflink. I spied wide-leg barrel leg jeans constructed in a patchwork of subtly different blue washes. My favorite piece was a pair of very long cargo shorts cut in tropical wool, with functional buttons that travel from the hems all the way up to just below the waistband. Most of the collection was made in New York, with some cut-and-sew done in Los Angeles and a few knits made in Italy.

Chow: Max and I used to work together at Sean John. That’s where we met and that’s where we established our friendship. blocks.x: Why take the hiatus and why bring the brand back now?

It really flew by, but we always knew that we would get back to it, and it was like, “Hey, let’s just take the time that we need to really get back to it in a meaningful and thoughtful way.”

Osborne: Fashion has changed.

blocks.x: As native New Yorkers, how do you feel about the way New York City has changed over the last decade or so?

All the economic recovery that happened afterwards certainly changed the landscape, accelerating all this new money and growth in the city, which definitely accelerated the gentrification of a lot of different neighborhoods. You had this push and pull of people who were born here, who built their businesses and families here, who had no choice to leave—and this new influx of money and private equity coming in, then adding their layer of what they think New York City should be.

Now, I think we’re going through a renaissance after Mamdani’s mayoral election. I’m a fan of his, and I think that he has really captured the spirit of what New York City is about, really helping all New Yorkers. Everyone lends a hand, everyone is part of a rebuild or helping each other get back on their feet. New York City is looking up.
